items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: I reviewed a lot of Edith Piaf repertoire

ctx.x: And do you sense, do you get a sense of the audience when you’re on stage? I’m not sure, do you feel a vibe or something, and may it direct the way you play?

It could. Sometimes I pre-think this. I played in a West Switzerland in the French area and here I reviewed a lot of Edith Piaf repertoire but I forgot about age. These were young people. They were bored stiff. I had a small handful, they seemed to disappear at intermission. I think somebody bought me a drink, maybe out of pity. But so I try, but of course I have been, I did more of my panel a day or two afterwards when I play in Tours, France for an audience that I’ve worked with for three — for days. I…
Okay. Well that’s a hard thing, and I think it’s even harder in a concert setting than it might be in a club. Sometimes you can catch a vibe in a club.
